text:
Luke Hughes is having the season people kept waiting for. At 23 he plays over 24 minutes a night, has 14 points in 21 games, and already matches last season's six goals. His last ten games brought ten points, capped by a three-assist night in Washington on Nov. 14. Dimitri Filipovic and Harman Dayal spent part of a PDOcast episode on the steps he has taken this season.

Some of the goal total is hot finishing, 12.5% shooting against a likely range of 5% to 8%, but his overall scoring rate sits right at the top of our talent range, not outside it. The skating is the engine: his speed bursts rank in the 96th percentile by NHL EDGE tracking, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile among defensemen for chances from the slot.

The question is the same one it has always been. The Devils get 54.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice, but about three points less than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 3% of defensemen for chances allowed last season. The offense is real. Watch his own end.
